1) INTRODUCTION 
As we know Civil servants (recruited by UPSC/MPSC) are leading our nation to the better tomorrow. 
Civil Services are the machinery which paves the way to achieve the ultimate goal of the Indian 
constitution – being a welfare state. But in a multi lingual and multi -cultural society like ours, every 
social entity is not significantly represented in the decision -making process like Civil Services. Reason 
being the fundamental right of equal opportunity is denied to many.  
Anjuman-I-Islam is also keen to endeavor to bring the socio -economically weaker sections of society 
into the Civil services and eventually support the ultimate goal of a welfare state that is just and based 
on equality. Need was felt to create a platform so that likeminded people can contribute to the cause.  
The Anjuman -I-Islam’s UPSC Academy (AIUPSC), a coaching centre for UPSC Civil services and other 
allied exams aims to empower the students/candidates of Muslim minority candidates, who are 
relatively disadvantaged secti on of our society. The success stories of many Muslim students drawn 
from various strata is a motivation for Anjuman -I-Islam, Mumbai to set up a coaching centre under its 
ambit. The coaching centre shall be made more comprehensive keeping in view the emerg ing trends of 
other coaching centres established by Hajj House, Jamia Millia, AMU, other Professional Coaching 
centres etc.  
2) OBJECTIVES

Vision: To be a humble inclusive academy for producing Nation building Civil Servants. 
Strategy: To assist the aspirants to frame an accurate an d separate strategy and plan at every level of 
examination, i.e. Preliminary, Mains and Interview.

The Civil Services Examination (abbr. CSE) is a standardised test in India conducted by the Union Public Service Commission (UPSC) for recruitment to higher civil services in the Government of India, such as the All India Services and Central Civil Services (Group A and a few Group B posts).[4] It is considered to be one of the toughest examinations in the world.[5][6][7]

It is conducted in three phases: a preliminary examination (abbr. Prelims) consisting of two objective-type papers (Paper I consisting of General Studies and Paper II consisting of Mathematics, Logical Reasoning and Comprehension, referred to as the Civil Service Aptitude Test or CSAT). The candidates who qualify the Prelims will appear in the main examination (abbr. Mains) consisting of nine papers of conventional descriptive type, in which two papers are qualifying and rest of the seven papers are accountable to qualify the Mains. Finally, after qualifying the Mains, a personality test (abbr. Interview) is conducted in the UPSC headquarters in New Delhi.[4][8] A successful candidate sits for 32 hours of examination during the complete process spanning around one year.

## List of services

[edit | edit source]

Those who pass the Civil Service Examination may be selected to join the following services:

* Indian Administrative Service (IAS)
* Indian Police Service (IPS)

* Central Civil Services (Group A)

* Indian Foreign Service (IFS)
* Indian Audit and Accounts Service (IAAS)
* Indian Civil Accounts Service (ICAS)
* Indian Corporate Law Service (ICLS)
* Indian Defence Accounts Service (IDAS)
* Indian Defence Estates Service (IDES)
* Indian Information Service (IIS)
* Indian Postal Service (IPoS)
* Indian P&T Accounts and Finance Service (IP&TAFS)
* Indian Railway Protection Force Service (IRPFS)
* Indian Revenue Service (IRS)
  + Indian Revenue Service (Income Tax) (IRS-IT)
  + Indian Revenue Service (Custom & Indirect Taxes) (IRS-C&IT)
* Indian Railway Management Service (IRMS)
* Indian Trade Service (ITrS)

* Central Civil Services (Group B)

* Armed Forces Headquarters Civil Services (AFHQCS)
* Delhi, Andaman and Nicobar Islands Civil Service (DANICS)
* Delhi, Andaman and Nicobar Islands Police Service (DANIPS)
* Pondicherry Civil Service (PONDICS)
* Pondicherry Police Service (PONDIPS)

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
DEPARTMENT OF HIGHER EDUCATION 
 
LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 57 
ANSWERED ON 21.07.2025 
 
Coaching Centers for Preparation of UPSC Examination 
 
57. Shri Adhikari Deepak Dev: 
 
Will the Minister of EDUCATION be pleased to state:  
(a) the number of coaching centers authorised by the Central Government for UPSC exam in the 
country; 
(b) the details of coaching centers being run for preparation of UPSC examination, State-wise; and 
(c) the action taken by the Government against unauthorised coaching centers, year-wise? 
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
(DR. SUKANTA MAJUMDAR) 
 
(a) to (c): Education is in the concurrent list, the State and UT Government need to take proactive 
action on the matter of Coaching Institutes. In order to regulate the Private Coaching and tuition 
classes, a number of States/UTs have brought out guidelines / regulations / legislations. Majority of 
these coaching centers spread across the country are commercial entities which need to be regulated 
as per the law of the respective States / UTs. Ministry of Education has also circulated a Guidelines 
for Regulation of Coaching Center to States/UTs on 16.01.2024. 
 
Department of Social Justice and Empowerment, Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment runs 
a Scheme namely Free coaching for SCs, OBCs and beneficiaries of PM CARES Children Scheme, 
for imparting coaching for competitive examinations for obtaining appropriate jobs in 
Public/Private Sector including Civil Services Examination and/or for securing admission in 
reputed technical and professional higher educational institutions. The Scheme is being 
implemented by Dr. Ambedkar Foundation through Dr. Ambedkar Centre of Excellence (DACE) 
established in empanelled Central Universities. As on date, a total of 19 Central Universities are 
empanelled under the Scheme.  
 
The Residential Coaching Academy (RCA) scheme was initiated in 2009 by University Grants 
Commission (UGC) to support students from Minority communities, SC/STs, and women by 
providing them with equal opportunities through specialized coaching. Launched in select central 
universities—Aligarh Muslim University (AMU), Maulana Azad National Urdu University 
(MANUU), Jamia Millia Islamia (JMI), Jamia Hamdard, and Babasaheb Bhimrao Ambedkar 
University—the scheme offers residential coaching for competitive exams, including Central/State 
Government services, banking, and private sector jobs. The scheme does not charge tuition fees but 
may levy nominal registration and hostel charges. 
 
Department of Consumer Affairs, the Central Consumer Protection Authority (CCPA) imposes 
penalty on coaching institutes for making misleading advertisements and directs them to 
discontinue such advertisements.
